expected_level_description: You can: - set how the organisation uses skills frameworks across professions - use skills data to inform workforce, learning, and reward strategy - contribute to the development of shared frameworks with other organisations

skill: Capability building for digital, data and technology
expected_level_description: *Senior leadership skill: the UK GDaD PCF defines it with one statement, not by level.* You can: - guide the organisation to ensure it has the specialist digital, data and technology skills it needs - develop organisational processes and ways of working so that digital and data roles you support can thrive - continuously improve and optimise the organisational environment Examples of leadership using this skill: - prioritising capability needs that will have the most impact - negotiating for longer-term investment in people by articulating the risks and benefits of different staffing strategies - advocating for good practice in ways of working and supporting people to adopt this practice - growing digital and data communities
You can: - analyse learning needs and design blended programmes to meet them - set learning outcomes and evaluate impact, not only satisfaction - make learning accessible and inclusive for all staff
You can: - collect and check workforce plan data from managers - model simple scenarios, such as turnover and vacancy trends

You can: - write adverts that appeal to specialist candidates and use plain language - search job boards, professional networks, and talent pools for candidates - support events, such as careers fairs and open days

You can: - work with the team to develop and maintain an understanding of stakeholders - work with the team to develop and implement stakeholder communications strategies - identify and resolve issues, influence stakeholders and manage relationships effectively - build long-term strategic relationships and communicate clearly and regularly with stakeholders
You can: - line manage a team, setting objectives and running appraisals - support wellbeing and manage attendance, performance, and conduct - plan the team's development and succession
You can: - hold and manage a budget, forecasting and explaining variances - build a business case with costs and benefits

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
